terms.x: a pointer that owns and cleans up
terms.p: A value that points at something, owns it, and does extra work when it is dropped — freeing a buffer, decrementing a count, releasing a lock.

terms.x: the trait behind the star operator
terms.p: The trait a type implements to say what it points at, which is what makes the star operator and method lookup reach through it.
The compiler silently converting a reference to a pointer-like type into a reference to what it points at, repeatedly, until the expected type is reached.

terms.x: a handle that does not own
terms.p: A reference-counted handle that does not keep the value alive, and which must be upgraded to a strong handle before use — returning nothing if the value has already gone.
Two or more reference-counted values holding handles to each other, so each keeps the other's count above zero and neither is ever freed.
A wrapper allowing a value to be replaced through a shared reference by only ever copying whole values in and out, so no reference to the inside ever escapes.
Memory that stays allocated with nothing able to reach it, which wastes space but is not unsafe, so Rust permits it in safe code.
